summary.headline: Omnitech Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR175.56 crore; H1 revenue up 50% and order book about INR3,178 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue grew 40.5% YoY to INR175.56 crore, with EBITDA up 17.7% to INR51.25 crore and PAT up 35.5% to INR30.57 crore, so margins compressed. H1 FY27 revenue rose 50% YoY, with PBT up 117.3% to INR80.01 crore. Management guided full-year FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and EBITDA margin of 30-32%, and said the Chhapara expansion is due in about 10-11 months. The call also covered new defence, aerospace and data-centre order flow, but several answers on capacity and timing were loose.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: 53.5% of Q2 revenue and 76% of order book; management described the business as mainly operations and maintenance rather than capex-linked.

segments.name: Motion control and automation
segments.commentary: 22.9% of Q2 revenue and about 12% of order book.

segments.name: Industrial equipment systems
segments.commentary: 19.4% of Q2 revenue and about 11.5% of order book.

segments.name: Other diversified applications
segments.commentary: 4.2% of Q2 revenue; new data-centre and defence work sits in this and adjacent mix, with first commercial orders received.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% YoY; management said 40% would be welcome but is not the current estimate.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 30-32%; management cited a historical 30-33% range to sustain over about 3 years.
Q3 and Q4 margins expected to be in line with a 32-33% historical range for the full year (answer on profitability, which is ambiguous).
Order book expected to convert over about 5 years (Weatherford programme), with FY28 ramp-up and larger contribution in FY29-FY30.
Chhapara expansion to complete in about 10-11 months (behind schedule by 1-2 months); peak revenue potential stated at INR1,100-1,200 crore on about 2x asset turn.
Average borrowing cost around 8-8.25%; about INR210 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised, to be deployed on schedule.
capex_capacity: Annualised machine-hour capacity at Sept 30, 2026 was 3.34 million hours, up 26.2% from 2.65 million hours in FY26.
Current utilisation stated at about 68-71%; peak utilisation of 80-85% considered achievable.
Chhapara, Rajkot expansion under construction; commissioning in about 10-11 months.
IPO capex of INR418 crore: INR50 crore debt repayment done, about INR208 crore utilised, about INR210 crore unutilised.
Further capex of INR1,200 crore-scale considered for next 2-3 years from debt and internal accruals; Gujarat Viksit scheme being explored for funding.
demand_pricing: Approximately 89% of Q2 revenue from outside India; North America 65.5%, Asia 20.9%, India 10.8%, Europe and UK 2.8%.

Order book about INR3,178 crore as of Oct 31, 2026; mix of 1-3 year orders and a 5-year Weatherford programme; management indicated roughly INR600 crore a year as an oversimplification and said ramp-up would be gradual.
Raw material and currency movements are passed through to customers under contracts with a 5-8% band, reviewed quarterly or half-yearly; cancellation not part of the discussion for these orders.
Data-centre qualification takes 8-14 months; management said margins in data-centre work will not differ from current levels.
Aerospace and defence: first-article orders executed and approved; commercial production orders received; NADCAP certification in progress; in-house metallurgical lab NABL accredited under ISO 17025.
Q2 other expenses rose as a share of sales (about 28% per analyst) due to tooling, consumables, heat-treatment job work and new-capacity ramp-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 other expense increase as a share of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher tooling and consumables usage, job work such as heat treatment, and costs linked to new capacity ramp-up and new machines; expected to normalise over FY27 as Q3 and Q4 ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating leverage as it enters data-centre, defence and new segments, plus raw-material MOQ constraints and new product development; it expects a 30-33% historical margin range to hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from Chhapara capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak revenue of about INR1,100-1,200 crore could be reached, based on roughly 2x asset turn and 30-35% growth; it declined the analyst's INR1,400-1,500 crore figure.

qa_highlights.question: How was the INR3,178 crore order book expected to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders run from 1 to 5 years; dispatches begin this year and ramp through FY28, with larger volumes in FY29 and FY30 as new capacity commissions.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the IPO proceeds are used?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR418 crore IPO objects, INR50 crore went to debt repayment and about INR208 crore is utilised in total, with about INR210 crore still unutilised.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for a dedicated facility for end customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said discussions are ongoing with large OEMs but are too preliminary to disclose; it will only announce once confirmed.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin fell to the 29-30% range in recent quarters versus the historical 35-40% cited by an analyst; watch whether the 30-32% FY27 range holds.
Sequential slowdown: analyst cited QoQ revenue growth of 5.3% and PAT growth of 2.8%.
Chhapara expansion timeline has already slipped 1-2 months; any further delay affects FY28 ramp-up.
Data-centre and defence qualification cycles of 8-14 months and NADCAP timing could defer revenue.
Other expenses elevated as a share of sales; management expects normalisation in H2 FY27 but has not quantified it.
Management answers on IPO fund deployment, EBITDA-margin basis and H1 PAT figures were imprecise; verify against the financial results filing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order book, but cautious and sometimes vague on margins, timelines and specific end-applications; management declined to name defence customers and called facility discussions premature.
key_quotes: The first half of FY27 reflects continued momentum in Omnitech's growth journey.
So, once the well is operational, usually you keep on requiring components, product lines and so on and so forth.
All INR600 crores won't be executed this year.

adds.what: Chhapara, Rajkot expansion (under construction), peak revenue potential INR1,100-1,200 crore

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% (midpoint 32.5%) with EBITDA margin 30-32%, backed by a 3.34 million machine-hour capacity (up 26.2%), 68-70% utilisation with spare headroom, a INR3,178 crore order book, and the Chhapara expansion due in 10-11 months (1-2 months late), though capacity and timing answers were loose.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin about 29% (INR51.25 cr on INR175.56 cr) fell YoY and QoQ, and management guides FY27 EBITDA margin only 30-32% with other expenses elevated (~28% of sales per analyst) and tooling/job-work costs expected to normalise only gradually.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chhapara, Rajkot expansion is under construction with INR208 cr of IPO capex already utilised and commissioning guided in 10-11 months, though it is already 1-2 months behind schedule; annualised machine-hour capacity is already up 26.2% to 3.34 million hours.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% (midpoint 32.5%) with H1 revenue up 50%, a INR3,178 cr order book, and utilisation at only 68-71% leaving spare headroom before the 80-85% peak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Further capex of about INR1,200 cr-scale is considered over the next 2-3 years, with Gujarat Viksit scheme funding being explored, and utilisation at 68-71% suggests the next large plant is still a planning-stage item rather than an immediate trigger.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said 40% growth would be welcome but is not the current estimate, versus guidance of 30-35%, and H1 revenue is already up 50%, so an upgrade is possible if H2 holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Chhapara has already slipped 1-2 months, data-centre and defence qualification takes 8-14 months, and QoQ revenue growth slowed to 5.3% with PAT growth at 2.8%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Data-centre and defence work sits in the Other diversified segment (4.2% of Q2 revenue) with first commercial orders in hand, but NADCAP certification is still in progress and qualification takes 8-14 months.

rows.label: INR3,178 cr order book converting over 1-5 years
rows.why: Order book of INR3,178 cr as of Oct 31, 2026 (76% Energy) with dispatches starting this year, ramping through FY28, and larger contribution in FY29-FY30; management said the INR600 cr a year figure is an oversimplification.

rows.label: Defence and aerospace qualification
rows.why: First-article orders are approved and commercial production orders received, with NADCAP certification in progress and an NABL-accredited lab, but customers are undisclosed and qualification takes time.

rows.label: Gujarat Viksit funding for next capex
rows.why: Management is exploring Gujarat Viksit scheme funding for the next INR1,200 cr-scale capex from debt and internal accruals, with about INR210 cr of IPO proceeds still unutilised.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, FY27 growth guidance of 30-35% and Chhapara capacity, but cautious and vague on margins, commissioning timelines and end-customers; analysts pressed on the margin decline, other expense spike, sequential slowdown and the Chhapara peak revenue figure.
